extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, PTAB practitioners, and patent attorneys handling claim construction and IPR appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for construing patent claims and evaluating whether a tribunal (particularly the PTAB) has implicitly or explicitly construed claims, and the proper appellate standards and APA notice requirements when the Board adopts a claim construction. Focuses on use of intrinsic evidence, presumptions about separately-listed claim elements, and when remand is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims define scope of the patented invention
rubrics_metrics.description: “claims of a patent define the scope of a patented invention and the patentee’s right to exclude.” Claims are 'the life of the patent,' defining the limits of the patent’s scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use claims to determine the patent’s scope because that scope must be known for protection of the patentee and encouragement of others; treat claim language as central in any scope analysis (citing Teva, Markman, Philips, Gen. Elec.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction serves to define scope and is a judicial statement
rubrics_metrics.description: “Claim construction serves to define the scope of the patented invention and the patentee’s right to exclude.” A claim construction is the judicial statement of what is and is not covered by the technical terms and other words of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize when an analysis is determining the meaning/boundaries of claim terms — that is claim construction — regardless of label the tribunal uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary reliance on intrinsic evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: “When construing claim terms, we first look to, and primarily rely on, the intrinsic evidence, including the claims themselves, the specification, and the prosecution history of the patent, which is usually dispositive.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve construction disputes primarily from the intrinsic record; only consult extrinsic evidence if intrinsic sources are inconclusive. Treat specification and prosecution history as potentially dispositive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of review: de novo for construction; substantial-evidence for underlying facts
rubrics_metrics.description: “We review the issue of claim construction of a patent claim de novo with any underlying fact findings reviewed for substantial evidence.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On appeal, claim construction is reviewed de novo (cases cited). Factual findings supporting construction or application to facts are reviewed for substantial evidence; properly distinguish which standard applies to each aspect of the tribunal’s decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine whether a tribunal has construed a claim by whether its analysis established scope/boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: “To determine whether a court, or the Board, has construed a claim, it is helpful to look to the outcome of the tribunal’s analysis. If the outcome ... establishes the scope (e.g., boundaries) and meaning of the patented subject matter, the court (or the Board) has most likely construed the claim.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the tribunal says it did not construe a claim, examine whether its findings effectively established claim scope (citing Netword, HTC, Trading Techs.). If so, treat it as claim construction for purposes of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separately listed claim elements create a presumption of distinctness
rubrics_metrics.description: “Where a claim lists elements separately, the clear implication of the claim language is that those elements are distinct components of the patented invention.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the presumption that separately recited elements denote distinct components (citing Becton, Engel), but do not treat this presumption as absolute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of distinctness is rebuttable by the intrinsic record/specification
rubrics_metrics.description: “There is a ‘presumption’ that separately listed claim limitations may indicate separate and distinct physical structure, but that presumption may always be rebutted in the context of a particular patent.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claim language or the specification contemplates embodiments where one claimed input is calculated from another (or otherwise intertwines elements), that intrinsic evidence can rebut the presumption of distinctness (examples and citations: Powell, specification §§).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not interpret claims to exclude embodiments disclosed in the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: “We normally do not interpret claim terms in a way that excludes embodiments disclosed in the specification.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claim construction reads claims to encompass embodiments expressly disclosed in the specification unless the patentee clearly disavowed that scope; a construction that excludes such embodiments is likely erroneous (citing Oatey).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee’s selection of broad terms yields broad plain-and-ordinary-meaning scope absent disavowal
rubrics_metrics.description: “A patentee ‘is free to choose a broad term and expect to obtain the full scope of its plain and ordinary meaning unless the patentee explicitly redefines the term or disavows its scope.’”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor a broad, plain-and-ordinary-meaning construction unless the intrinsic record shows an explicit redefinition or disavowal by the patentee (citing Thorner).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim differentiation is a guide, not a rigid rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctrine of claim differentiation only creates a rebuttable presumption that each claim in a patent has a different scope; it is a guide, not a rigid rule of claim construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not mechanically apply claim-differentiation to restrict scope; evaluate whether intrinsic evidence rebuts the presumption (citing Curtiss‑Wright).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribunal may adopt a construction neither party proposed but must afford APA notice and opportunity to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Board may adopt a claim construction of a disputed term that neither party proposes without running afoul of the APA.” However, the Board cannot, without notice and opportunity for the parties to respond, change theories midstream by adopting a claim construction in its final written decision that neither party requested nor anticipated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board’s construction was not proposed by the parties, ensure the record shows the parties had notice of the contested construction issue and an opportunity to address it; otherwise APA violation may require reversal (citing Qualcomm, SAS, Hamilton Beach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language like 'based at least in part on' places no constraint on manner inputs are used
rubrics_metrics.description: In the ’753 claim the phrase that a time is determined 'based at least in part on' each of five inputs 'places no constraint on the manner in which the inputs are used.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claim language uses broad linking phrasing (e.g., 'based at least in part on'), prefer a construction that permits interdependence among inputs unless the specification or prosecution history indicates otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit constructions and the necessity to examine whether parties litigated the issue
rubrics_metrics.description: A tribunal can implicitly construe a claim even if it states it did not, and an implicit construction does not violate the APA if the parties had notice of the contested claim construction issues and an opportunity to be heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the record for whether the parties disputed the scope/meaning of the claim term during proceedings; if the issue was squarely presented, the tribunal's implicit construction is less likely to be an APA problem (examples in the record).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy when Board's construction is erroneous: reverse, vacate, and remand
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board’s claim construction is erroneous, the proper disposition is to reverse the Board’s construction, vacate the Final Written Decision, and remand for further proceedings under the correct construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On appellate review, correct legal error in claim construction by remanding so the tribunal can apply the correct construction to its unpatentability/factfinding analysis.
